reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: CABG x3 plus AVR on a patient whose platelets fell from 218 to 96 on 24 days of heparin (HIT never tested) heading for full heparinization, clopidogrel washout of only 3 days, an unaddressed pacemaker, and lisinopril given this morning.

asa.rationale: Severe AS with three vessel CAD, NYHA III, EF 45%, CKD.

decision.recommendation: hold until HIT is evaluated and the device plan is set
decision.rationale: A platelet drop over 50% on prolonged heparin makes HIT plausible, and CPB needs 400 units/kg heparin. Send PF4 antibody (and SRA if positive), stop heparin if suspicion holds, and plan bivalirudin if HIT is confirmed. Clopidogrel last 10/24 also missed the 5 day washout.

redFlags.finding: Possible heparin induced thrombocytopenia before full heparinization
redFlags.evidence: Platelets 218 to 112 to 104 to 96 on a heparin infusion since 10/03; hematology suggested HIT workup; PF4 ELISA not ordered.
redFlags.implication: Heparin for CPB in active HIT risks catastrophic thrombosis.
redFlags.action: PF4 antibody now (SRA if positive), calculate a 4T score, stop heparin and use an alternative (bivalirudin) if HIT is likely.

redFlags.evidence: Ordered held 5 days but last dose 10/24; surgery 10/27; platelets 96.
redFlags.action: Platelets available, consider platelet function testing or delay; antifibrinolytic per protocol.

redFlags.evidence: Medtronic dual chamber, AP 38%, underlying sinus 50s; rep not called; interrogation and reprogramming not ordered.
redFlags.action: Interrogate, reprogram to asynchronous mode for the case (or magnet DOO 85), external pads, re interrogate postop.

redFlags.finding: ACE inhibitor given the morning of CPB
Severe AS with three vessel CAD
redFlags.evidence: AVA 0.7, mean gradient 44, LAD 85%, LVEDP 22, EF 45%.
redFlags.implication: Induction hypotension or tachycardia can start an ischemic spiral.
redFlags.action: Arterial line before induction, maintain SVR and sinus rhythm, phenylephrine ready, slow induction.

redFlags.evidence: Carotid duplex 10/07; vascular: higher MAP on bypass, cerebral oximetry.
redFlags.action: Cerebral oximetry, higher MAP targets on CPB.

redFlags.evidence: Cefazolin plus vancomycin due within 60 min of incision.
redFlags.implication: Vancomycin needs to start 60 to 120 min before incision.

planItems.item: Arterial line pre induction, PA catheter, TEE
Heparin 400 units/kg with ACT over 480 s unless HIT; TXA per protocol
Cell saver, 4 units crossmatched, platelets available
Cefazolin within 60 min, vancomycin started 60 to 120 min before incision
